ai-at-work.title: Amazon responds to data center backlash, says it no longer uses NDAs
ai-at-work.excerpt: The CEO of Amazon Web Services tried to push back against widespread suspicion of data centers.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Amazon says it's ditching NDAs that prevented customers from disclosing data center locations and security practices. This matters because digital workplace leaders choosing cloud infrastructure need transparency about where their data actually lives and how it's protected, especially for compliance and risk management. After years of operating like a tech speakeasy where you couldn't even tell people which region you were in, Amazon finally figured out that opacity isn't a selling point. Better late than never, I guess.

ai-at-work.title: OpenAI safety employee resigns, claiming the company’s ‘culture is broken’
ai-at-work.excerpt: By his own admission, David Robinson is “something of a cliché”: an employee at a leading AI company who issues a dire warning while resigning from their job.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: David Robinson quit his safety role at OpenAI and publicly claimed the company has a broken culture that won't listen to safety concerns. This matters because if the outfit building one of the world's most powerful AI systems can't keep its own safety staff from fleeing, that's a legitimate red flag for anyone banking on AI governance working as intended. Look, we've seen this movie before with other tech giants, and it never ends with "actually everything was fine."

ai-at-work.title: All the AI agents that can live in your text messages
ai-at-work.excerpt: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: TechCrunch rounded up AI agents that now operate directly within text messaging platforms, giving users quick access to various specialized assistants without jumping between apps. This matters because your employees are already living in messaging apps, so AI agents that meet them there could finally make those tools useful instead of just another notification stream to ignore. The real question is whether workers will actually want AI agents pestering them via SMS or if we're just trading one cluttered inbox for another, but at least the notifications will be slightly smarter this time around.

ai-at-work.title: 9 insights from ‘Private Tech Trailblazers’: Vertical AI becomes the growth engine
ai-at-work.excerpt: The companies featured at the recent Bank of America Private Tech Trailblazers Conference point to where the next wave of AI growth is taking shape: specialized technology built around proprietary dat
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Vertical AI is eating the tech world's lunch, with specialized AI built for specific industries and workflows replacing generic tools as the real growth driver. This matters because your digital workplace strategy that relies on one-size-fits-all platforms is already looking tired compared to these purpose-built alternatives. Here's the kicker: most organizations will spend the next two years trying to retrofit their existing tech stacks instead of admitting they should have gone vertical from day one.

tools-tech.title: ServiceNow launches standalone AI service desk to provide support in Teams, Slack, and email
tools-tech.excerpt: ServiceNow has a new take on the service desk: Flow by ServiceNow, a standalone AI product that allows users to get help via chats in Microsoft Teams, Slack, or a Flow web app, or by email, rather tha
tools-tech.dwp_take: ServiceNow launched Flow, a standalone AI service desk that handles support requests through Teams, Slack, email, and a web app without forcing users to leave their workflow. This matters because IT leaders are finally getting a tool that actually meets employees where they work instead of demanding they jump through hoops to submit a ticket. The real test will be whether Flow can actually solve problems or if it just becomes another chatbot that escalates everything to a human while pretending it understood the question.

digital-culture.title: This anti-scam checklist can protect you against the latest AI-enhanced frauds
digital-culture.excerpt: Recently, I received an email solicitation from a PR company offering to help me promote my book. While I get these kinds of solicitation emails on occasion, this one impressed me with the level of de
digital-culture.dwp_take: Someone got a weirdly detailed phishing email that seemed personalized but was actually AI-generated spam. For digital workplace folks, this matters because your employees are getting these same convincing AI scams in their inboxes right now, and traditional "don't click suspicious links" training isn't cutting it anymore. The real kicker is that AI is getting good enough at research that it can flatter us into lowering our guard, which means your security training needs to shift from spotting bad grammar to spotting suspiciously good attention to detail.

digital-culture.title: Trump’s Crazy AI Rebrand Was a Loyalty Test for Tech Execs—and It Worked
digital-culture.excerpt: For years these billionaires gushed obsessively about AI. But they meekly went along when Trump canceled the term.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Trump pushed tech executives to stop using the term "artificial intelligence" and rebrand it as "StarGate," and most of the industry complied without pushback. This matters to digital workplace pros because it shows how quickly corporate messaging discipline crumbles when pressure comes from above, and how buzzwords that supposedly define entire business strategies can evaporate overnight if leadership decides they're inconvenient. After three decades watching workplace tech trends, I can tell you this is the most transparent loyalty test I've seen since executives started calling layoffs "rightsizing," and it should worry anyone betting their career on whatever the current AI narrative happens to be.

industry-news.title: Google Launches AI Chips Into Orbit to Test Space Data Centers
industry-news.excerpt: Google’s Project Suncatcher launches AI chips into orbit to test radiation resistance, cooling, and whether space data centers could become practical. The post Google Launches AI Chips Into Orbit to T
industry-news.dwp_take: Google shot AI chips into space to see if data centers could actually work up there, testing how they handle radiation and cooling in orbit. For digital workplace folks, this matters because data latency and processing speed directly affect employee experience, so space-based computing could theoretically revolutionize how we access applications and services. Look, I've seen enough pie-in-the-sky tech pitches to know that "testing in space" is either a genuine engineering breakthrough or the most expensive way ever to avoid fixing earthbound infrastructure problems.

industry-news.title: Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra vs iPad Pro With M5: Which Premium Tablet Gives You More?
industry-news.excerpt: Samsung's Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra offers a larger display, included S Pen, and expandable storage, while the iPad Pro with M5 leads in performance and battery life. The post Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra vs iPad
industry-news.dwp_take: Samsung's Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Apple's iPad Pro M5 are duking it out in the premium tablet space, with Samsung offering a bigger screen and stylus while Apple flexes on raw performance and battery life. For digital workplace folks, this matters because you're probably fielding requests from executives who want tablets that can actually replace laptops, and now you've got real trade-offs to explain instead of just saying "get an iPad." Honestly, if your org isn't already tired of buying tablets that gather dust in desk drawers, you will be soon, which is why this comparison feels like arguing over which luxury car to leave in the parking lot.

industry-news.title: Tencent Reportedly Turns to Southeast Asia for $7B Oracle AI Chip Deal
industry-news.excerpt: Tencent reportedly plans to lease about 100,000 AI chips from Oracle in Southeast Asia under a five-year deal worth roughly $7 billion. The post Tencent Reportedly Turns to Southeast Asia for $7B Orac
industry-news.dwp_take: Tencent is reportedly leasing 100,000 AI chips from Oracle through Southeast Asian entities in a roughly $7 billion deal, apparently navigating around US export restrictions on advanced semiconductors. This matters because it shows how geopolitical chip constraints are reshaping where companies source computing infrastructure, which directly affects where AI workloads and data processing happen for digital workplace tools. If your company's AI features depend on chip availability in specific regions, you're about to learn that geography is your destiny whether you like it or not.

industry-news.title: Vietnam’s AI Adoption Jumps to 26%, but Most Adopters Are Still Experimenting
industry-news.excerpt: Vietnam AI adoption hit 26%, but most adopters are still experimenting as skills, ROI measurement, and regulation slow production deployments. The post Vietnam’s AI Adoption Jumps to 26%, but Most Ado
industry-news.dwp_take: Vietnam's enterprise adoption of AI has reached 26%, but most organizations are still in the "poking around" phase rather than actually putting AI into production. This matters to digital workplace pros because it confirms what we're seeing globally: companies are excited about AI but hitting real walls on skills gaps, measuring actual value, and figuring out the regulatory landscape. Basically, we've got a lot of organizations running expensive AI science projects that probably should be called pilot programs, but hey, at least they're trying.
